SERVICE-HOME-01.fail_or_repair: Do not treat a metropolitan or regional body as a service home until the service map and service promise owner are visible.
SERVICE-HOME-01.label: Territorial service map
SERVICE-HOME-01.question: Does the packet state which services stay local, which are shared, which are directly operated, and which remain state or national before naming a service home?

SERVICE-HOME-02.fail_or_repair: Open an operator-chain docket and reject governance-by-board or governance-by-contractor shorthand.
SERVICE-HOME-02.label: Authority, operator, regulator, commissioner, contractor split
SERVICE-HOME-02.question: Can the packet distinguish who sets the service obligation, who commissions, who operates, who regulates or inspects, who contracts, and who hears unresolved complaints?

SERVICE-HOME-03.fail_or_repair: Downgrade the service-home claim to memorandum-network posture until the lawful delivery instrument is identified.
SERVICE-HOME-03.label: Lawful delivery instrument
SERVICE-HOME-03.question: Does the shared tier have a lawful instrument to commission, franchise, directly operate, enforce, intervene, or step in rather than only a strategy or memorandum?

SERVICE-HOME-04.fail_or_repair: Do not accept back-end integration as service government until user entry, handoff, and remedy routes are visible.
SERVICE-HOME-04.label: Near-to-person front door and handoff
SERVICE-HOME-04.question: Can ordinary users enter through accessible local or common channels and see where unresolved matters move next when the back end is shared?

SERVICE-HOME-05.fail_or_repair: Treat the service home as incomplete until failure-takeover and continuity obligations survive partner exit.
SERVICE-HOME-05.label: Continuity, substitution, and failure takeover
SERVICE-HOME-05.question: If a municipality, operator, concessionaire, vendor, or contractor fails, who still owes the territory the service and what reserve, substitution, or transition path exists?

SERVICE-HOME-06.fail_or_repair: Reject service-home claims where each operator carries a separate promise, separate data rhythm, and separate complaint path.
SERVICE-HOME-06.label: Operator-chain public service constitution
SERVICE-HOME-06.question: Are common service obligations, reporting, incidents, interoperability, data, performance disclosure, and fallback responsibility declared across the operator chain?

SERVICE-HOME-07.fail_or_repair: Do not treat a board packet, statute, operator report, audit, or map as proof that the user actually received service.
SERVICE-HOME-07.label: Source boundary and outcome proof
SERVICE-HOME-07.question: Does the packet separate authority documents, operator reports, board papers, audits, complaints, and lived service outcomes before scoring service continuity?

SERVICE-HOME-08.fail_or_repair: Keep the old route active until the successor can show source/test/protected-element parity.
SERVICE-HOME-08.label: Route-absorption parity
SERVICE-HOME-08.question: Before retiring an older service-home route, does the successor route preserve the protected elements, generated tests, source keys, case example, and redirect path?
